title: Geometric normal-slice comparison for supported cohomology
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], with arbitrary $n\geq1$. Let $S$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $T\to X$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $Y_T=Y\times_XT$ [def-pc-base-change], and suppose there is an etale $S$-morphism $h:T\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$, for integers $a,b\geq0$ [def-sbc-affine-space], with $Y_T=h^{-1}(\mathbf A^a_S)$ scheme-theoretically, where the coordinate subspace is cut out by the last $b$ coordinates. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], write $R\underline\Gamma_{Y_T}$ for the right derived functor [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] of the sheaf of sections with support: for an abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and an etale object $W\to T$, put $Y_W=Y_T\times_TW$; the underived sheaf assigns $\ker(F(W)\to F(W\setminus Y_W))$. For every $r\in\mathbf Z$ and geometric point $\bar t$ on $Y_T$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], there is a coordinate-induced isomorphism of complexes of $A$-modules
$$\bigl(R\underline\Gamma_{Y_T}(A(r))\bigr)_{\bar t}\simeq R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^b_k,A(r)),$$
where the right side is ordinary etale supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology], $\{0\}$ is the origin, and twists are [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The comparison is compatible with further etale restriction of $T$ and with the identifications of twists $A(r)=A(b)\otimes_A A(r-b)$. If there is a fixed integer $c\geq0$ such that $\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}=\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}+c$ for every $y\in Y$, with Krull dimension defined as the supremum of lengths of strict prime chains, then every such chart with $Y_T\ne\varnothing$ has $b=c$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, for the geometry; Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, for supported derived sections. The geometric normal-slice comparison over an arbitrary k-base is an agent-formulated auxiliary assertion, not a theorem asserted by either of these tags. Over the base field itself (S = Spec k, X and Y smooth k-varieties) the corresponding assertion is Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorem 16.7 (cohomological purity: R^r i^! F = 0 for r != 2c, R^{2c} i^! F = (i^*F)(-c)) with the etale-local standard model of Lemma 16.8, printed pp. 111--112 (literature/milne-lectures-on-etale-cohomology_LEC.pdf); Milne proves it by induction from the case m=c=1 of his 14.3. The arbitrary-base form is not cited from any SGA volume.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $S_0$ of the image of $\bar t$, put $B=\mathbf A^a_{S_0}$ and view the chart as etale over $P=\mathbf A^b_B$. For every finitely generated $k$-subalgebra of the affine base ring, [lem-pur-finite-type-coordinate-support-orientation] identifies the stage support complex with $z_*A(r-b)[-2b]$; at a geometric point on the zero section the stalk of a closed direct image is the stalk of the sheaf on the closed subscheme by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar], and the stalk of the constant line sheaf is $L_{r-b}$. So the stage supported stalk cohomology is $L_{r-b}$ in degree $2b$ and zero otherwise. Its base-change compatibility makes the transitions the identity on $L_{r-b}$. Apply [lem-pur-affine-coordinate-support-stalk-continuity] in each degree: the same concentration and ordered coordinate identification hold over $B$. Its normalization and refinement clauses identify this orientation with pullback of the field coordinate class and make it independent of the affine models.

source.place: Assembly of the separately stated arguments extracted from original Steps 1--4 and the refinement part of Step 7.

proof.text: Over $k$, [lem-pur-finite-type-coordinate-support-orientation] identifies the global supported complex with $L_{r-b}[-2b]$. The chart and Step 1 now satisfy the two concentration hypotheses of [lem-pur-concentrated-support-etale-transfer]. Before applying it, shrink $T$ to the open $T_0=h^{-1}(\mathbf A^{a+b}_{S_0})$, which contains $\bar t$: etale inverse image along $T_0\hookrightarrow T$ is literal restriction [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], under which the support kernel of $Y_T$ restricts to that of $Y_T\times_TT_0$ on every etale test object; restriction is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and preserves injectives [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], so it carries $R\underline\Gamma_{Y_T}$ to the derived support kernel on $T_0$, and the stalk at $\bar t$ is unchanged by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar]. Applied to the etale map $T_0\to P$, [lem-pur-concentrated-support-etale-transfer] identifies the actual derived support kernel on the chart, proves the normalized global-to-stalk morphism invertible, and identifies its inverse with the functorial truncation comparison. Inverting gives the displayed isomorphism. The transfer lemma supplies further etale restriction and twist compatibility; the continuity lemma in Step 1 supplies independence of the chosen affine neighbourhood and finite stages. The empty product covers $b=0$, and empty support has no geometric points at which to make an assertion.

source.place: Assembly of the separately stated arguments extracted from original Steps 5--7 and the field part of Step 6.

proof.text: If $Y_T$ is nonempty, apply [lem-pur-coordinate-chart-finite-dimension-witness] to $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$, $e:T\to X$ and $h$. It gives $y\in Y$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,y}=0$ and $\dim\mathcal O_{X,y}=b$, both finite. At this point the additional hypothesis reads $b=0+c$, hence $b=c$. No cancellation of infinite local dimensions is involved.

source.place: Assembly of the separately stated arguments extracted from original Steps 8--9.
